breaking.headline: FAA ground-stop fallout: 5,000+ flights canceled Saturday; copper-to-fiber upgrade blamed
breaking.fact: Federal officials said Saturday the nationwide ground stop likely stemmed from an L3Harris contractor upgrading aging copper telecom lines to fiber at a remote FAA site, affecting 17 of 22 air-traffic control centers; more than 5,000 Saturday flights were canceled and 10,000+ delayed or canceled, with full recovery expected Sunday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is seeking $50 billion to modernize air-traffic control, warning the aging system 'will continue to break until we replace it.' The stop, lifted at 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, was the longest nationwide halt in 25 years and the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11.

breaking.headline: Anthropic IPO six times oversubscribed; banks shut out China and Hong Kong investors
breaking.fact: Bloomberg reported orders for Anthropic's IPO reached about six times the shares on offer, with bankers prioritizing existing backers; banks have also refused orders from institutional investors in mainland China and Hong Kong under U.S. arms-export rules, after the prospectus noted some AI products could fall under ITAR. Terms are unchanged — 825 million shares at $70–$78, up to $64.4 billion, pricing Wednesday Nov 18, trading Thursday as ANT — and Nvidia reports Q3 results Tuesday at about 1:20 p.m. PT, its first under interim CEO Colette Kress.

breaking.headline: Trump says no Iran deal needed, pulls Vance off negotiations
breaking.fact: President Trump said Thursday the U.S. “doesn’t need a deal with Iran” and directed Vice President JD Vance — who led the earlier talks — to focus instead on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities; the administration signals the naval blockade and sanctions are working, so neither further military escalation nor diplomacy is needed. The war, now in its ninth month, has upended Middle East oil flows and cost 23 U.S. service members’ lives.

breaking.headline: Bitcoin falls below $70,000 for first time since August as crypto sells off
breaking.fact: Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August, trading near $65,000–$67,000 on Saturday as crypto sold off broadly — Ether down about 6%, Solana about 7% — and the Crypto Fear & Greed Index collapsed to 13, extreme fear; the slide tracks the week’s AI-trade nerves and speculation around the Anthropic IPO.

weekInBrief.headline: Fed survey: AI is now the top risk to the financial system
weekInBrief.body: The Federal Reserve’s semi-annual Financial Stability Report, released Friday, found AI the top-cited risk among the 23 market contacts surveyed in September and October — 87% named it, up from 50% in May and 30% a year ago — citing stretched valuations, AI-related financing and cyber risks; advanced-computing debt issuance has surged to $680 billion, about five times 2023’s level.

weekInBrief.headline: Goldman Sachs sees 2.8% global growth in 2027, led by the AI boom
weekInBrief.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts global economic growth of 2.8% in 2027, with the U.S. expanding 2.4% and the U.K. 1.4%, driven by the AI investment boom — a relatively upbeat call issued into a week when the same AI trade was rattling markets.

weekInBrief.headline: Amazon revives deal with troubled Fermi data-centre venture
weekInBrief.body: Fermi, the Texas data-centre developer co-founded by former U.S. energy secretary Rick Perry, signed a 600-megawatt power deal with an unnamed hyperscaler the Financial Times identified as Amazon, including a $200 million prepayment and a $15 million pre-construction agreement; work on the Amarillo site starts by Dec. 1, a reversal after talks collapsed last December. Fermi still reported a $141.6 million third-quarter loss and holds $286 million in cash against $958 million in debt.

weekInBrief.headline: China’s producer prices jump 5.7%, fastest in over four years
weekInBrief.body: China’s producer price index jumped 5.7% in October, its fastest pace in over four years, driven by mining, raw materials and external demand, even as new bank lending slipped for the third time this year — down about 100 billion yuan — on weaker credit demand from households and businesses.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: CENTCOM said Saturday it shot down two Iranian one-way attack drones over Bahrain after Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed it had destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar there; U.S. forces reported no injuries or damage. Tehran’s claims of three tankers striking mines in the strait remain unconfirmed, with no vessel names or flags given and CENTCOM calling the accounts “false.” The blockade is also widening onto land: CENTCOM’s Task Force Iron Gate, announced Nov. 7, is pressing Iran’s neighbors to choke off overland trade, though Iraq, Turkey and Pakistan are resisting closing border crossings. On oil, CENTCOM says the naval blockade has now prevented more than $25 billion in Iranian crude exports, Kpler’s tracking still shows zero Iranian crude loadings since late August, and non-Iranian crude keeps moving through the strait at about 7.3 million barrels a day.

space.headline: Mechazilla catches Ship 42 — first-ever catch of a Starship upper stage
space.body: At about 3:20 p.m. CT Saturday, Ship 42 settled into the launch tower’s arms at Starbase after 22.5 hours and 14 orbits — the first time a Starship upper stage has ever been caught; SpaceX confirmed “Mechazilla catches Starship!” All 26 Starlink V3 satellites were deployed and contacted. The booster catch failed Friday — Booster 22 called off its own return on a guidance problem after a low fuel-mass alarm ended its boostback burn early, and exploded above the Gulf.

space.headline: Voyager 1 closes in on one light-day from Earth
space.body: On Wednesday, Nov. 18, NASA’s Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth — more than 16 billion miles out, its radio signals taking exactly 24 hours to reach us. NASA is inviting people to flash a wave of golden light after sunset Tuesday, spelling V-G-R in Morse code. Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 has been in interstellar space since 2012; its twin won’t reach the mark until 2035.

space.headline: Monthly shot helps children tolerate peanuts
space.body: A monthly immunotherapy shot, PVX108, helped children with peanut allergy tolerate far more peanut in a Phase 2 trial of 71 children aged 4 to 11: on the higher dose, 39.4% tolerated at least 443 mg of peanut protein against 16.7% on placebo, and the benefit held six months after treatment stopped, with no treatment-related anaphylaxis. Full data were presented at the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology meeting on Saturday; the treatment is investigational and not yet approved.

space.headline: Liver drug’s year-long results, now peer-reviewed
space.body: Pemvidutide, an investigational drug for the fatty liver disease MASH, kept improving liver measures at 48 weeks in results published Nov. 12 in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology: 32.4% of patients on the higher dose hit a combined liver-stiffness and fibrosis-marker target against 3.2% on placebo, alongside significant weight loss, in a 212-person trial. About 1% stopped treatment because of side effects, and a global Phase 3 trial is already running, with its main readout expected in 2029.

apod.title: Rigel and the Witch Head Nebula
apod.credit: Piotr Czerski — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 9, 2026
apod.explanation: The Witch Head Nebula (IC 2118) spans about 50 light-years of gas and dust, partly eroded by the nearby blue supergiant Rigel in Orion; its blue glow comes from Rigel’s intense starlight and from dust grains scattering blue light more efficiently than red.
